title: Collateral Protection Insurance Refund Terms — Cancellation of Placed Coverage, Closure and Refund Destinations
content:
These terms govern refunds of Collateral Protection Insurance premium and the closing of a tracking record. Two clauses are marked below as no longer in force; they are superseded by the current basis.

## 1. One refund per charge

A premium charge can be refunded only once.

## 2. Full refund on continuous coverage

When accepted proof shows coverage effective on or before the coverage effective date of the placed coverage with no gap, every premium charge of the placement is refunded in full (refund basis: full, no lapse).

## 3. Refund from the proof's effective date

*Retired clause — no longer in force:* the clause under which, when accepted proof starts after the placed coverage's effective date, each unrefunded charge is refunded for the days of its billing period on or after the proof's policy effective date, the days before that date staying earned (refund basis: pro rata from proof effective). This clause is superseded by the current basis.

## 4. Refund on closure

*Retired clause — no longer in force:* the clause under which, when the record closes because the contract left active servicing while force-placed, each unrefunded charge is refunded for the days of its billing period after the contract's closed date (refund basis: pro rata from closure). This clause is superseded by the current basis.

## 5. Amount and rounding

A full refund is the charge's amount. A prorated refund is the charge's amount multiplied by its refundable days and divided by its period days. The period days are the calendar days from the first day through the last day of the charge's billing period, both included. The refundable days are the days of that period falling on or after the refund start date (the accepted proof's policy effective date, or, on closure, the day after the contract's closed date), both ends included, and are 0 when the start date is after the period's last day. Every refund is rounded half-up to the cent.

**Hypothetical:** a USD 100.00 charge for a 30-day period with 12 refundable days refunds USD 100.00 multiplied by 12 and divided by 30, that is USD 40.00.

## 6. Held premium

A held premium is released by a held-premium release refund for its full amount, with the disposition "not-billed release", because it never reached the contract.

## 7. Timing and destination

Refunds of capitalised premium are issued within the product's refund processing period and go to the first applicable destination in the product's destination order:

| Contract situation | Destination |
|---|---|
| Contract active, repossessed or charged off | credited to the contract balance |
| Contract liquidated and its deficiency account not closed | credited to the deficiency balance |
| Any other situation | mailed to the borrower by check to the mailing address on file |

A mailed refund below the product's smallest check amount is not issued.

## 8. Closing a tracking record

A tracking record closes when its contract leaves active servicing (paid off, unwound, liquidated or charged off), on the contract's closed date. A repossessed contract's record stays open but is not billed.
